title: FlashSaleHoldResult
description: Published by Seat Inventory Service after executing (or choosing not to execute) the Redis Lua script for a FlashSaleHoldRequest. Consumed by: Booking Service (saga advancement) and Notification Service (WebSocket push to customer). Partition key: customerId — avoids hotspot on popular events, enables ordered delivery per customer.

messageId.description: Consumer deduplication key (NFR-REL-002). A replayed HOLD_SUCCEEDED must not trigger duplicate payment initiation. Booking Service must check booking.status != PENDING before acting: if already processed, ack and discard.

customerId.description: Partition key for this topic. Avoids hotspot on popular eventIds.

result.description: HOLD_SUCCEEDED: All seats atomically held. Booking proceeds to payment (ADR-005 Step 2). HOLD_FAILED: At least one seat unavailable. No seats held. Booking transitions PENDING→CANCELLED. HOLD_EXPIRED: Request arrived after expiresAt. Lua not executed. Booking transitions PENDING→CANCELLED.

holdId.description: Present only when result=HOLD_SUCCEEDED. Same semantics as gRPC HoldSeatsResponse.hold_id.

heldUntil.description: Present only when result=HOLD_SUCCEEDED. Redis TTL expiry = processedAt + 600s. Notification Service displays this as the checkout countdown timer.

unavailableSeats.description: Seats that blocked the hold (result=HOLD_FAILED). Empty array when result=HOLD_SUCCEEDED or HOLD_EXPIRED. Notification Service includes these in the hold-denied WebSocket event so the UI can highlight unavailable seats.

processedAt.description: UTC timestamp when the Seat Inventory consumer processed this request.

correlationId.description: Propagated from the original FlashSaleHoldRequest. Enables end-to-end trace: POST /bookings → hold-requests → hold-results → saga continuation.
